The exhibit shows a role in Manage roles. Geography relates one-to-many to Customer, which relates one-to-many to Sales.

What does a member of the Germany role see?

image.alt: Manage security roles: the Germany role is selected, the Geography table is selected, and its DAX filter is [Country] = "Germany".

options.text: All data, because the filter is on a dimension
Only the Geography table, filtered to Germany
No data, because Sales isn't filtered
Only German customers and their sales

questions.explanation: The filter keeps only German rows in Geography, and it flows from the one side to the many side: Geography → Customer → Sales. Members see German customers and their sales only.
questions.takeaway: RLS filters flow along relationships like any other filter.

questions.stem:
Your model has a dynamic role that filters on USERPRINCIPALNAME (). You want to check in Power BI Desktop what amira@contoso.com would see.

What should you select in the View as dialog shown in the exhibit?

image.alt: View as roles dialog with check boxes for None, Other user (with an email box), SalesRep (dynamic) and Executives.

options.text: The SalesRep role and Other user, entering amira@contoso.com

questions.explanation: Tick the dynamic role and tick Other user, entering amira@contoso.com. USERPRINCIPALNAME () then returns that email, so you see exactly her data. Ticking only the role would use your own identity.
questions.takeaway: Test dynamic RLS for someone else → View as: role + Other user.

questions.stem: Which function should a dynamic RLS filter use to compare a table's Email column with the signed-in user, so it behaves the same in Power BI Desktop and the service?
questions.explanation: USERPRINCIPALNAME () returns the user principal name (usually the work email) in both places. USERNAME () returns DOMAIN\user in Desktop on a domain-joined machine, so tests in Desktop may not match the service.
questions.takeaway: Dynamic RLS → USERPRINCIPALNAME ().

questions.stem:
Employee has EmployeeID, ManagerID, Email and Path = PATH ( Employee[EmployeeID], Employee[ManagerID] ). Managers must see their own rows and those of everyone below them.

Which role filter on Employee should you use?
questions.explanation: PATHCONTAINS checks whether each employee's path (their chain of managers) contains the signed-in user's EmployeeID, looked up from their email. That returns the user and everyone under them at any level.
questions.takeaway: Hierarchical RLS → PATH + PATHCONTAINS with the user's ID.

questions.stem: For each statement about RLS, select Yes if it is true.
statements: A user assigned to two roles sees the rows allowed by either role.
Workspace Contributors aren't restricted by RLS.
RLS applies to a user with Build permission who connects through Analyze in Excel.
questions.explanation: A user in several roles sees the union of what each role allows. Workspace Admins, Members and Contributors can edit the model, so RLS doesn't restrict them. RLS does apply to Viewers and to people with only Build permission, including when they use Analyze in Excel.
questions.takeaway: Roles combine as a union; editors bypass RLS; Viewers and Build-only users don't.

questions.stem:
Store managers have a dynamic role. The CFO must see every store, and is a workspace Viewer.

What should you do?

options.text: Do nothing; Viewers see everything by default
Create a role with no filter and add the CFO to it
Make the CFO a workspace Contributor
Add the CFO to the store managers' role

questions.explanation: Once RLS exists, a Viewer in no role sees no data. Create a role with no filter (or a TRUE () filter) and add the CFO to it. Making the CFO a Contributor would grant editing rights just to bypass security.
questions.takeaway: Full-access users under RLS → a role with no filter.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a model. A role filters Users with [Email] = USERPRINCIPALNAME (), but members still see every region's sales.

What should you do?

image.alt: Model view: Region relates one-to-many to Users and one-to-many to Sales, with single-direction filters flowing from Region to each.

options.text: Move the role filter to Sales
Change the role to use USERNAME ()
Set Users–Region to Both and select Apply security filter in both directions
Mark Users as a date table

questions.explanation: Users is on the many side of its relationship with Region, so the filter on Users doesn't flow to Region and on to Sales. Set that relationship to filter in both directions and select Apply security filter in both directions, so the security filter reaches Region and then Sales.
questions.takeaway: Security filter on a many-side mapping table → Both + Apply security filter in both directions.

questions.stem: Where do you add people or security groups to an RLS role after publishing?

options.text: On the semantic model's Security page in the Power BI service
In Power BI Desktop's View as dialog

questions.explanation: In the Power BI service, open the semantic model's Security page, select the role and add members. Roles themselves are defined in Power BI Desktop.
questions.takeaway: Assign role members → semantic model > Security in the service.

questions.stem:
Analysts must build their own reports on a semantic model protected by RLS, and RLS must still restrict what they see.

How should you grant access?

options.text: Grant Build permission on the semantic model without an editing workspace role

questions.explanation: Workspace Contributors and above bypass RLS. Give the analysts Build permission on the semantic model (and keep them as Viewers or outside the workspace): they can create reports in their own workspace, and RLS applies to them.
questions.takeaway: Build reports + stay restricted → Build permission, not an editor role.

questions.stem:
You share a report with a colleague who isn't a member of any RLS role on the semantic model.

What does the colleague see?

options.text: Only data from the default role
The data visible to the person who shared it

questions.explanation: Sharing grants access to the report, but RLS still decides which rows they see. Belonging to no role means no rows, so visuals show no data.
questions.takeaway: Sharing doesn't bypass RLS; no role = no data.

questions.stem:
After assigning members, you want to confirm in the Power BI service what a role shows.

What should you use?

options.text: Test as role on the semantic model's Security page

questions.explanation: On the semantic model's Security page, the role's menu has Test as role, which opens the report as a member of that role would see it (and lets you test as a specific person).
questions.takeaway: Test RLS in the service → Security > Test as role.

questions.stem:
Some sales reps cover several regions, and the list changes often. You need dynamic RLS by region.

How should you store who can see what?

options.text: A mapping table with one row per user and region
A comma-separated list of regions in each user's row

questions.explanation: A mapping table with one row per user per region (Email, RegionKey) handles any number of regions per person, and changes only need new rows, not new roles. A single region column in a user table can't hold several regions.
questions.takeaway: Users with several allowed values → one row per user per value in a mapping table.

questions.stem: Where should an RLS filter usually be defined for best performance and clarity?

options.text: On the dimension table that identifies the user's scope

questions.explanation: Filter the small dimension (for example Region or Customer) and let relationships carry the filter to the fact. Filtering a large fact table row by row is slower and repeats logic for every fact table.
questions.takeaway: Put RLS filters on dimensions.

questions.stem: A semantic model uses RLS. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
statements: Dashboard tiles pinned from the report respect RLS for each viewer.
You can share the report publicly with Publish to web, and RLS still applies.
Answers from Q&A respect RLS.
questions.explanation: Dashboard tiles and Q&A answers run against the model as the viewer, so RLS applies. Publish to web isn't available for reports that use RLS, because it would expose data publicly without identity.
questions.takeaway: RLS follows the user everywhere they query the model; Publish to web is blocked.

questions.stem:
You create a report with a live connection to a shared semantic model that uses RLS.

What applies to your report's viewers?

options.text: No RLS, unless you recreate the roles in your report

questions.explanation: RLS is part of the semantic model, so it applies to every report built on it, including live-connected ones. You can't add or change roles from a live-connected report.
questions.takeaway: RLS lives in the semantic model and follows every report built on it.

questions.stem: You secure the Salary column with object-level security (OLS) for every role except HR. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
statements: Non-HR users can't see or query the Salary column.
A visual that uses Salary shows an error for non-HR users.
OLS filters Employee rows by department.
questions.explanation: OLS hides the column from users without access, as if it didn't exist; visuals that use it show an error for them. It doesn't filter rows, which is RLS's job.
questions.takeaway: OLS hides tables/columns; RLS filters rows.

questions.stem: Select the feature that meets each requirement.

parts.label: Regional managers see only their region's rows
Only HR can see the Salary column
Exported files stay encrypted and marked Confidential

questions.explanation: RLS restricts rows per user. OLS hides tables or columns. Sensitivity labels classify content and keep protection on exported files.
questions.takeaway: Rows → RLS. Columns/tables → OLS. Classify and protect exports → sensitivity labels.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows two years of monthly revenue as a column chart. Managers say it's hard to see the overall trend and the seasonal pattern.

Which visual should replace it?

image.alt: Column chart with 24 monthly bars from January 2025 to December 2026, rising through the year with peaks each December.

questions.explanation: A line chart joins consecutive months, so the trend and the yearly seasonal shape are easy to follow. Columns for 24 periods emphasise individual months rather than movement over time. Pie and treemap visuals show part-to-whole, not change over time.
questions.takeaway: Change over time, many periods → line chart.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
You need to compare sales across 12 product categories with long names, so that users can quickly see which categories sell most.

Which visual should you use?

options.text: Bar chart sorted by sales descending

questions.explanation: A horizontal bar chart has room for long labels, and sorting it by sales descending makes the ranking obvious. A pie chart with 12 slices is hard to compare; a line chart implies a sequence that categories don't have.
questions.takeaway: Compare many categories → bar chart, sorted.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem: Select the visual that best meets each requirement.

parts.label: Share of revenue from three sales channels this year
How each channel's share changed over 12 months
How price, volume and cost changes moved profit from last year to this year

questions.explanation: A donut (or pie) works for a part-to-whole with only a few parts. A 100% stacked column shows how shares change across periods. A waterfall shows how increases and decreases build from a starting value to an ending value.
questions.takeaway: Few-part share → donut. Share over time → 100% stacked. Build-up of changes → waterfall.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows sales by region per year. Users want to compare each region's share of the yearly total, but the totals change every year.

What should you change?

image.alt: Stacked column chart for 2023 to 2026 with North, South and West segments. Total sales grow every year, from 270 to 535.

options.text: Change it to a 100% stacked column chart
Change it to a clustered column chart
Sort the axis by total sales

questions.explanation: A 100% stacked column chart scales every year to 100%, so the segments show each region's share and are directly comparable across years. A clustered chart compares absolute values; adding data labels doesn't fix the changing totals.
questions.takeaway: Compare shares across categories with different totals → 100% stacked.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
The exhibit plots stores by sales (x-axis) and profit margin (y-axis).

Which store has high sales but an unusually low margin?

image.alt: Scatter chart: stores A, B, C, E and F cluster at 190 to 400K sales with 26 to 37% margin; Store D sits at 610K sales and 9% margin.

questions.explanation: Store D sits far to the right (high sales) but near the bottom (low margin), away from the cluster of other stores. That separation is exactly what a scatter chart is good at revealing.
questions.takeaway: Scatter charts show relationships and outliers between two measures.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
You need to show monthly revenue (in millions) and profit margin % (between 8% and 15%) in one visual, each readable on its own scale.

What should you use?

image.alt: Line and clustered column chart: revenue columns from 2.1 to 3.3 million on the left axis and a margin % line between 9% and 15% on a right-hand secondary axis.

options.text: A clustered column chart with both measures
A line and clustered column chart, with margin % on the secondary axis

questions.explanation: A line and clustered column chart (combo) shows revenue as columns on the primary axis and margin % as a line on a secondary axis, so both scales stay readable. On one shared axis the percentage line would sit flat at the bottom.
questions.takeaway: Two measures with very different scales → combo chart with a secondary axis.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
You're building a KPI visual that compares this month's sales with the sales target and shows the monthly trend.

Select the field for each well.

parts.label: Indicator
Trend axis
Target

questions.explanation: Indicator is the value being evaluated, Trend axis is the field the background trend uses (usually a date field), and Target is what the indicator is compared against. The visual colours the value by whether it meets the target.
questions.takeaway: KPI visual: Indicator = value, Trend axis = time, Target = goal.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a KPI visual. Higher values are better.

What does it tell you?

image.alt: KPI visual showing 412K in red with the text Goal: 450K (-8.4%) and a shaded trend in the background.

questions.explanation: The indicator (412K) is below the goal (450K) by 8.4%, which is why it's shown in red. The shaded background is the trend over the trend axis.
questions.takeaway: KPI visual: colour = meeting or missing the target.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a gauge.

Which statement is true?

image.alt: Gauge from 0 to 1M with the arc filled to 620K and a target marker at 750K.

options.text: The gauge shows a trend over time
Current value is 620K, below the 750K target

questions.explanation: The gauge runs from 0 to 1M, the filled arc shows the current value of 620K, and the marker shows the target of 750K, so the value hasn't reached the target yet.
questions.takeaway: Gauge: value arc, min/max range and target marker.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
Sales leadership wants to see how many opportunities move through each stage: Lead, Qualified, Proposal, Negotiation and Won.

Which visual should you use?
questions.explanation: A funnel chart shows a sequence of stages, each narrower than the last, making drop-off between stages visible. A waterfall shows increases and decreases to a total, not stage conversion.
questions.takeaway: Sequential stages with drop-off → funnel.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
You need to shade each state on a map by total sales, darker for higher sales.

Which visual should you use?

options.text: Map with bubbles sized by sales

questions.explanation: A filled map (choropleth) shades whole geographic areas by value. A basic map places bubbles at locations; a scatter chart has no geography.
questions.takeaway: Shade areas by value → filled map.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
An executive page must show Revenue, Profit, Orders and Margin % together as headline numbers in one compact visual.

Which visual should you use?

options.text: A card visual with all four measures

questions.explanation: The card visual can display several callout values (one per measure) in a single visual, so related headline numbers stay aligned and formatted together. A gauge or KPI visual shows one measure.
questions.takeaway: Several headline numbers together → card visual with multiple values.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
You need the same line chart of monthly sales repeated for each of eight regions, with shared axes so users can compare them.

What should you use?
questions.explanation: Small multiples split one visual into a grid of mini charts, one per region, with consistent axes, and new regions appear automatically. Eight separate charts would need maintaining and could drift apart in scale.
questions.takeaway: Same chart per category → small multiples.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem: Select the slicer setup that meets each requirement.

parts.label: Always show the last 30 days, rolling forward each day
Pick a unit price range from 10 to 50
Pick one of 300 customers by typing part of the name

questions.explanation: A relative date slicer keeps a rolling window such as the last 30 days. A Between (range) slicer lets users pick a numeric range. A dropdown slicer with search suits long lists such as 300 customers.
questions.takeaway: Rolling dates → relative date. Ranges → Between. Long lists → dropdown with search.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a line chart with a shaded forecast.

Where is the forecast configured, and what does the shaded area represent?

image.alt: Line chart of sales from January to September, followed by a dashed forecast line for three more months inside a shaded band that widens over time.

options.text: The Analytics pane; the shaded area is the confidence interval
The Format pane; the shaded area is last year's sales
The Filters pane; the shaded area is filtered-out data
A quick measure; the shaded area is the running total

questions.explanation: Forecast is added from the Analytics pane of a line chart with a continuous date axis. The dashed line is the predicted value; the shaded band is the confidence interval around it.
questions.takeaway: Forecast → Analytics pane, line chart with continuous dates; band = confidence interval.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows sales by representative with an average line from the Analytics pane.

How many representatives are above the average?

image.alt: Column chart of sales by representative: Ahmed 41, Bianca 61, Chen 74, Dev 38, Elena 40, Farah 58, with a dashed average line at 52.

questions.explanation: The dashed average line sits at 52K. Bianca (61K), Chen (74K) and Farah (58K) are above it; the other three are below.
questions.takeaway: Analytics lines are calculated from the data in the visual.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a waterfall chart of profit from last year to this year.

Which factor reduced profit the most?

image.alt: Waterfall from last year's profit of 500K: Price +60K, Volume +45K, Cost of goods −90K, Returns −25K, ending at 490K this year.

questions.explanation: Red bars are decreases. Cost of goods (−90K) is the largest drop; returns took off 25K. Price and volume increased profit.
questions.takeaway: Waterfall: green = increase, red = decrease, blue = totals.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
In the exhibit, the bars for two regions look very different, but their sales are almost the same.

What should you change?

image.alt: Column chart where the axis starts at 900K: North at 960K looks less than half the height of South at 985K.

options.text: Set the value axis to start at 0

questions.explanation: The value axis starts at 900K, which exaggerates small differences. Setting the axis to start at 0 shows the bars in proportion to their values.
questions.takeaway: Bar and column axes should start at zero.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
Product sales range from 100 to 2,000,000. On a column chart, most products look like empty bars next to the biggest ones.

Which axis setting helps users compare them?
questions.explanation: A logarithmic scale spaces values by orders of magnitude (100, 1K, 10K…), so small and large values are both readable. Note that log scales can't show zero or negative values.
questions.takeaway: Values spanning orders of magnitude → logarithmic axis.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem: The exhibit shows a table visual. Which conditional formatting option produced the horizontal bars in the Sales column?

image.alt: Table of Sales by Product with blue bars inside the Sales cells and green, red and amber icons in the Trend column.

questions.explanation: Data bars draw a bar inside each cell, proportional to the value. Background colour shades the cell; icons add symbols; field value takes a colour from a field or measure.
questions.takeaway: Bars inside cells → data bars.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem: Select the conditional formatting style for each requirement.

parts.label: Red below 90% of target, amber to 100%, green above
Shade from light to dark as sales increase
Use the hex colour returned by a [Status Colour] measure
Show an up or down arrow beside each value

questions.explanation: Rules apply colours by thresholds (red/amber/green). Gradient shades from low to high. Field value uses a colour a field or measure returns. Icons add symbols such as arrows.
questions.takeaway: Thresholds → Rules. Smooth shading → Gradient. Colour from a measure → Field value. Symbols → Icons.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A chart's title must read 'Sales for North' or 'Sales for South' depending on the selected region.

What should you do?

options.text: Type both titles and hide one
Use the fx button on the title and pick a measure that returns the text
Add the region to the legend

questions.explanation: Create a measure that builds the text (for example with SELECTEDVALUE), then select the fx button next to the visual's Title text and choose that measure. Many formatting properties accept a measure this way.
questions.takeaway: Dynamic titles → fx on Title text with a text measure.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
In a column chart, bars for products below target must be red and the others blue.

What should you do?

options.text: Use fx on the column colour with a rule or a colour measure

questions.explanation: Under Columns > Colours, select fx and use Rules or Field value with a measure such as a below-target flag or colour measure. Moving a field into Legend would colour by category, not by a condition.
questions.takeaway: Colour bars by a condition → fx on the series colour.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A column chart of sales by month skips months that had no sales. Users must see every month, including empty ones.

What should you do?

options.text: Turn on Show items with no data for the Month field

questions.explanation: Turn on Show items with no data for the Month field in the visual's field well. Months without sales then appear with no bar instead of disappearing.
questions.takeaway: Show empty categories → 'Show items with no data'.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A product table must show a small line of each product's monthly sales trend inside each row.

What should you add?

options.text: A line chart beside the table

questions.explanation: Sparklines in tables and matrices draw a tiny chart per row, for example sales over Month. They're added from the Values well's menu (Add a sparkline).
questions.takeaway: Mini trend per row → sparkline.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A matrix has several measures, and users want each measure on its own row instead of as columns.

Which setting should you change?

options.text: Turn on Switch values to rows
Transpose the data in Power Query

questions.explanation: In the matrix's Format pane, under Values, turn on Switch values to rows. Each measure then appears as a row under the row headers.
questions.takeaway: Measures as rows in a matrix → Switch values to rows.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A matrix shows Category and Product indented in one column. Users want Category and Product in separate columns, like a spreadsheet.

What should you change?
questions.explanation: Turning off Stepped layout (Row headers in the Format pane) shows each hierarchy level in its own column instead of indenting levels in one column.
questions.takeaway: Separate columns per row level → turn off stepped layout.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
You've formatted one chart's colours, fonts and borders carefully and want another chart to look the same.

What is the quickest way?
questions.explanation: Format painter copies formatting from one visual to another in one click. Themes set defaults for the whole report rather than copying one visual's settings.
questions.takeaway: Copy one visual's formatting → Format painter.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
Some users are colour-blind and can't tell the red and green status colours apart.

What should you do?

options.text: Add icons or labels so meaning doesn't depend on colour

questions.explanation: Don't rely on colour alone: add data labels, icons (such as arrows), markers or patterns, and choose colours with good contrast. Changing the theme only helps if the new colours are distinguishable, and still relies on colour.
questions.takeaway: Never rely on colour alone to convey meaning.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
Screen-reader users need a description of what each chart shows.

What should you set?
questions.explanation: Alt text (in the visual's General settings) is read by screen readers. It can be static or built from a measure so it describes the current values.
questions.takeaway: Screen readers read a visual's alt text.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
IT wants report authors across the organisation to use only a few approved custom visuals, available to everyone without each author importing them.

What should you do?

options.text: Ask each author to import the visual from a file
Add them as organizational visuals in the admin portal
Put them in a report theme

questions.explanation: Power BI admins can add approved visuals as organizational visuals in the admin portal; they then appear for everyone in the visuals pane. Importing from a file per report doesn't centralise control.
questions.takeaway: Approved custom visuals for everyone → organizational visuals.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem: Select the filter level for each requirement.

parts.label: Only one chart should exclude returned orders
Every page must show only the current year
Only the Europe page should show European countries

questions.explanation: Visual-level filters affect one visual, page-level filters every visual on a page, and report-level filters every page.
questions.takeaway: Visual → one visual. Page → one page. Report (all pages) → everything.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A bar chart must show only the 10 customers with the highest sales.

What should you use?

options.text: A visual-level Top N filter on Customer, by Sales
A page-level basic filter on Customer

questions.explanation: A Top N filter on Customer, by the Sales measure with Show items: Top 10, in the visual's filters keeps the ten largest customers for the current context.
questions.takeaway: Top 10 in one visual → visual-level Top N filter.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A chart has a Top 10 customers filter by Sales. A user selects Asia in a Region slicer.

What does the chart show?

options.text: The overall top 10, filtered to those in Asia

questions.explanation: Top N is evaluated in the current filter context, so it shows the top 10 customers within Asia. To always rank across all regions, you'd need a measure-based approach.
questions.takeaway: Top N filters respect other filters.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
You need to show only customers whose Sales measure is above 10,000.

At which level can you filter on the measure's value?
questions.explanation: Filters on measure values are available only at visual level, because a measure's value depends on the visual's grouping. Page and report filters work on columns.
questions.takeaway: Filtering by a measure's value → visual-level filter.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A page must always show the previous three complete calendar months, updating automatically.

Which filter should you use on the Date column?

options.text: A basic filter with three months ticked
An advanced filter with fixed dates
A Top N filter on Date
A relative date filter: last 3 calendar months

questions.explanation: A relative date filter set to 'is in the last 3 calendar months' rolls forward automatically and uses complete months. A basic or advanced filter on fixed dates would need manual updates.
questions.takeaway: Rolling periods → relative date filter.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows the Filters pane. Report readers must not change the Year filter, and shouldn't see the Internal flag filter at all.

What should you do?

image.alt: Filters pane with a page filter on Region and two all-pages filters: Year is 2026 and Internal flag is False.

options.text: Lock the Year filter and hide the Internal flag filter

questions.explanation: Lock the Year filter so readers can see but not change it, and hide the Internal flag filter so it isn't shown in reading view. Both settings are on each filter card.
questions.takeaway: Visible but fixed → lock. Invisible → hide.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A matrix shows categories with a Category → Product hierarchy. Users want to see every category with its products listed underneath at once.

What should they use?

options.text: Expand all down one level in the hierarchy
Go to the next level in the hierarchy

questions.explanation: Expand all down one level in the hierarchy shows the next level for every category at the same time, keeping the category rows. Drill down shows only one category's products.
questions.takeaway: See every parent with its children → Expand all down one level.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A button must open the company intranet page about the sales process.

Which action type should you set?
questions.explanation: The Web URL action opens a web address. Page navigation, bookmark and drillthrough actions only move within the report.
questions.takeaway: Open a website from a button → Web URL action.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A visual shows the message 'Too many values. Not showing all data.'

What should you do?

options.text: Filter or summarise the field so fewer data points are needed

questions.explanation: Power BI reduces the data points it plots for very high-cardinality fields. Filter or summarise the field (for example a Top N filter or a coarser level) so the visual shows a meaningful amount of data.
questions.takeaway: 'Too many values' → filter or summarise to fewer data points.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
Users export data from a matrix and need all the detail columns from the underlying rows, not just the matrix's grouped totals.

Which export option should they choose?
questions.explanation: Underlying data exports the detail rows behind the visual's values. Summarized data exports what the visual shows. Admins and model owners can restrict underlying data export.
questions.takeaway: Detail rows → Underlying data. Visual's numbers → Summarized data.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
Users need to drill into a chart by clicking a column, moving from Year to Quarter for the clicked year.

What must be true?

options.text: The axis holds a Year → Quarter hierarchy and drill mode is on

questions.explanation: The axis must hold a hierarchy (or several fields), and drill mode must be on (the single down-arrow in the visual header). Clicking a column then drills into that year.
questions.takeaway: Click-to-drill needs a hierarchy on the axis and drill mode on.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
A report page shows a slicer for Region. On a second page, you need the same selection applied automatically, without showing the slicer there.

What should you do?

options.text: Copy the slicer and hide it
Sync the slicer to the second page without making it visible

questions.explanation: In the Sync slicers pane, tick the second page under Sync but leave it unticked under Visible. The selection applies there without the slicer appearing.
questions.takeaway: Apply a slicer's selection elsewhere without showing it → sync, not visible.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
The report must look good on phones in portrait orientation.

What should you create?

options.text: A mobile layout for each page

questions.explanation: A mobile layout (View > Mobile layout) arranges selected visuals for portrait phone screens. The Power BI mobile app uses it automatically.
questions.takeaway: Phone-friendly report → mobile layout.

questions.topic: Create reports: choose, build and format visuals
questions.stem:
You want a consistent header, logo position and grid for every new page in a report.

What helps most?

options.text: Build one template page and duplicate it for each new page
Use a different theme per page

questions.explanation: Duplicating a template page that already has the header, logo and layout (plus a report theme for colours and fonts) keeps every new page consistent. Themes don't place objects like logos on pages.
questions.takeaway: Consistent page layout → duplicate a template page (with a theme).

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows the Selection pane. You need one button that shows the chart and hides the table, and another that does the reverse.

What should you create?

image.alt: Selection pane listing Sales chart (visible), Sales table (hidden), Show chart button and Show table button.

options.text: Two bookmarks capturing different visibility, each assigned to a button

questions.explanation: Create two bookmarks: one captured with the chart visible and the table hidden (eye icons in the Selection pane), the other the reverse. Assign each to a button's Bookmark action. Turn off the Data property if users' slicer choices should be kept.
questions.takeaway: Show/hide visuals with buttons → Selection pane + bookmarks.

questions.stem: Select the bookmark property that controls each behaviour.

parts.label: Reapplies slicer and filter selections
Reapplies which visuals are shown or hidden
Takes the user to the page the bookmark was created on

questions.explanation: Data captures filters, slicers and sort order. Display captures visibility and spotlight/focus mode. Current page decides whether applying the bookmark also navigates to the page it was captured on.
questions.takeaway: Data = filters. Display = visibility. Current page = navigation.

questions.stem:
A bookmark should affect only the three visuals in a chart group, leaving other visuals on the page as they are.

What should you do when updating the bookmark?

options.text: Select the visuals and set the bookmark to apply to Selected visuals

questions.explanation: Select the three visuals, then set the bookmark to apply to Selected visuals (instead of All visuals). Only those visuals' state is captured and reapplied.
questions.takeaway: Limit a bookmark's effect → Selected visuals.

questions.stem:
Report readers in the Power BI service want to save their own filter combinations and return to them later, without the report author creating bookmarks.

What should they use?
questions.explanation: Personal bookmarks let each reader capture their own view (filters, slicers, visual state) in the service and choose one as their default. Report bookmarks are created by the author and shared with everyone.
questions.takeaway: Readers' own saved views → personal bookmarks.

questions.stem:
You've grouped five bookmarks named after regions. You want a set of buttons, one per bookmark, that updates automatically when bookmarks in the group change.

What should you insert?

options.text: A bookmark navigator for the group

questions.explanation: A bookmark navigator (Insert > Buttons > Navigator > Bookmark navigator) creates one button per bookmark in the selected group and updates when the group changes. Building buttons one by one needs manual upkeep.
questions.takeaway: Buttons for a bookmark group → bookmark navigator.

questions.stem:
Report pages are added and renamed often. You want navigation buttons for every page that stay up to date without editing.

What should you insert?

options.text: One button per page with a Page navigation action

questions.explanation: A page navigator creates a button for each page (optionally excluding hidden pages) and updates as pages are added, removed or renamed.
questions.takeaway: Automatic page buttons → page navigator.

questions.stem:
In Power BI Desktop, clicking a button doesn't trigger its action while you're editing.

How do you test the action?

options.text: Publish first; buttons only work in the service

questions.explanation: In Desktop editing mode, Ctrl+click a button to run its action (a plain click selects it for editing). In the service, a normal click works.
questions.takeaway: Test buttons in Desktop → Ctrl+click.

questions.stem:
You need users to right-click a product in any visual and open a Product Details page filtered to that product.

Select the actions you should perform and arrange them in order.

items.text: Create a page named Product Details
Add the Product field to that page's Drill through well
Add the detail visuals to the page
Create a bookmark for each product
Set the page as a tooltip

questions.explanation: Create the target page, add Product to its Drill through well (which also adds a back button), and build the detail visuals. Users then right-click a product anywhere and choose Drill through > Product Details. Bookmarks and tooltips aren't needed.
questions.takeaway: Drillthrough: target page + field in the Drill through well.

questions.stem:
A Customer Details report is separate from the Sales report, but both use the same semantic model. Users must right-click a customer in the Sales report and open the details report filtered to that customer.

What should you enable?
questions.explanation: Cross-report drillthrough: turn on Allow visuals in this report to use drillthrough targets from other reports in the source report, and set the target page's drillthrough to cross-report. Both reports must use the same semantic model (in the same workspace or app).
questions.takeaway: Drill into another report → cross-report drillthrough.

questions.stem:
Users drill through from a page that has Year and Region slicers set. The target page must respect both selections, not only the drilled-on product.

Which setting on the target page controls this?
questions.explanation: Keep all filters (on by default) passes every filter from the source visual and page into the drillthrough page. With it off, only the drillthrough field's value is passed.
questions.takeaway: Pass all source filters → Keep all filters.

questions.stem:
You want a mini chart of a product's monthly sales to appear when users hover over that product in any visual.

What should you build?
questions.explanation: A report page tooltip: a page set to Allow use as tooltip (usually with the Tooltip canvas size) containing the mini chart, with Product as its tooltip field. Visuals using Product then show it on hover.
questions.takeaway: Rich hover content → report page tooltip.

questions.stem:
When a user selects a month in a column chart, a card showing year-to-date sales must not change.

What should you do?

options.text: Add a visual-level filter to the card
Set the chart's interaction with the card to None

questions.explanation: Select the column chart, open Format > Edit interactions, and set the card's interaction to None. Other visuals can keep filter or highlight.
questions.takeaway: Stop one visual reacting to another → Edit interactions: None.

questions.stem:
Users want to Ctrl+click to select several columns in a chart and have other visuals filter to all of them.

What does Power BI do by default?

options.text: Multi-selection works by default, and other visuals respond to all selected points

questions.explanation: Ctrl+click (or Shift+click in some visuals) adds data points to the selection, and other visuals cross-filter or cross-highlight to the combined selection. No configuration is needed.
questions.takeaway: Ctrl+click = multi-select for cross-filtering.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a Key influencers visual analysing what makes a customer churn.

What does the top influencer mean?

image.alt: Key influencers visual: when Contract is Month-to-month, the likelihood of Churn being Yes increases 2.4 times; tenure under 6 months 1.9 times; more than 3 support tickets 1.6 times.

options.text: Customers on month-to-month contracts are 2.4 times more likely to churn
Month-to-month contracts cause 2.4 extra churned customers

questions.explanation: Customers with a month-to-month contract are 2.4 times more likely to churn than customers without that contract type. The right panel compares the churn rate for that group with everyone else.
questions.takeaway: Key influencers: 'When X, the likelihood increases by N times'.

questions.stem:
Instead of individual factors, you want Key influencers to find groups of customers with a combination of attributes that have a high churn rate.

Which tab should you use?
questions.explanation: The Top segments tab finds clusters of records defined by several attributes together (for example month-to-month contract and tenure under six months) where the outcome is much more common.
questions.takeaway: Combinations of factors → Top segments.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a decomposition tree. Its last level was added using an AI split.

Which AI split was used, and what does it do?

image.alt: Decomposition tree: total sales 1,240 split by Region (West 520 highlighted), then Channel marked High value (Online 330 highlighted), then Product (Trail Shoe 160).

options.text: High value: it chose the field with the highest value at that level
Low value: it chose the smallest contributor
Key influencers: it chose the strongest correlation
Top segments: it grouped similar customers

questions.explanation: The High value split picks, at that step, the field and value with the highest result, here the Online channel within the West region. Low value would pick the lowest.
questions.takeaway: Decomposition tree AI split: High value / Low value picks the next field for you.

questions.stem:
In a decomposition tree, you want AI splits to look for the biggest value relative to the other options at that level, rather than the absolute largest.

What should you change?

options.text: Set the AI split analysis type to Relative

questions.explanation: The analysis type can be Absolute (pick the highest value) or Relative (pick the value that stands out most compared with its siblings). Relative helps find unusually strong small segments.
questions.takeaway: AI split analysis type: Absolute vs Relative.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a line chart with anomaly detection turned on.

What do the circled points and the shaded band represent?

image.alt: Line chart of daily orders inside a shaded expected range. Day 7 (210 orders) and day 14 (60 orders) are circled outside the band.

options.text: Forecast values and their confidence interval
Anomalies outside the expected range shown by the band

questions.explanation: The band is the expected range calculated from the series; circled points fall outside it, so they're flagged as anomalies. Selecting one shows possible explanations based on the Explain by fields.
questions.takeaway: Anomaly detection: band = expected range, circles = anomalies.

questions.stem:
Anomaly detection flags too many points as unusual.

What should you change?
questions.explanation: Lower the sensitivity in the anomaly settings. Higher sensitivity flags smaller deviations; lower sensitivity widens the expected range so only bigger deviations count.
questions.takeaway: Too many anomalies → lower the sensitivity.

questions.stem:
When users select an anomaly, you want Power BI to suggest which categories, such as Region or Channel, might explain it.

What should you configure?

options.text: Explain by fields in the anomaly detection settings

questions.explanation: Add fields to Explain by in the anomaly detection settings. Power BI then ranks possible explanations, showing which values of those fields changed most at that point.
questions.takeaway: Explanations for anomalies → Explain by fields.

questions.stem:
Users see a sharp rise in one month on a column chart and want Power BI to find which categories contributed most, without building a new visual.

What can they use?
questions.explanation: Right-click the data point and choose Analyze > Explain the increase. Power BI looks across the model's fields for the biggest contributors and shows the results as visuals.
questions.takeaway: Why did this point rise? → Analyze > Explain the increase.

questions.stem: Select the visual that best answers each question.

parts.label: Which factors make an order more likely to be returned?
Where does this quarter's revenue come from, by region, channel and product?
Which days had unusually low website traffic?

questions.explanation: Key influencers ranks factors that drive an outcome. The decomposition tree breaks a total down step by step, letting users choose (or AI choose) the next level. A line chart with anomaly detection flags unusual points over time.
questions.takeaway: Drivers → Key influencers. Breakdown → decomposition tree. Unusual points over time → anomaly detection.

questions.stem:
Users type 'revenue by territory' in Q&A, but the model's measure is Sales Amount and the column is Region.

What should you add so Q&A understands them?

options.text: Synonyms for Sales Amount and Region

questions.explanation: Synonyms tell Q&A (and Copilot) that revenue means Sales Amount and territory means Region. Add them in Q&A setup or in the field's properties in Model view.
questions.takeaway: Users' words differ from field names → synonyms.

questions.stem:
An executive page needs an AI-written summary of its visuals that updates when slicers change.

What should you add?
questions.explanation: The narrative visual with Copilot generates a text summary of the page's visuals (or chosen visuals) and refreshes it as filters change. You can guide it with a custom prompt.
questions.takeaway: AI summary on a page → narrative visual with Copilot.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows the Copilot pane in Power BI Desktop.

What will Copilot do in response to this prompt?

image.alt: Copilot pane: the user asks to create a page that shows regional sales performance; Copilot replies that it has created a page with sales by region, a monthly trend and top products, with Keep it and Undo buttons.

options.text: Create a new report page with visuals about regional sales performance

questions.explanation: Asked to create a page, Copilot builds a new report page with visuals based on the semantic model and the prompt. You can then edit the page like any other.
questions.takeaway: Copilot can create report pages from a prompt.

questions.stem:
The Copilot pane is greyed out for a report in Power BI Desktop.

Which two conditions must be met for Copilot to be available? Choose the option that lists both.

options.text: A Pro licence and DirectQuery mode
Auto date/time and a marked date table
A certified semantic model and an app
The Copilot tenant setting turned on, and a workspace on a supported paid capacity

questions.explanation: Copilot needs the admin tenant setting that allows Copilot (Azure OpenAI features) and a workspace on a supported paid capacity, such as Fabric F2 or higher, or Premium P1 or higher. In Desktop you sign in and choose such a workspace. Pro licences on shared capacity don't provide Copilot.
questions.takeaway: Copilot = tenant setting on + supported paid capacity workspace.

questions.stem:
Your organisation's capacity is in a region where Azure OpenAI isn't available, and Copilot doesn't work.

What can an admin enable?

options.text: The setting that allows data to be processed outside your capacity's geographic region

questions.explanation: A tenant setting allows data sent to Azure OpenAI to be processed outside your capacity's geographic region. Turning it on lets Copilot work, subject to your organisation's data-residency rules.
questions.takeaway: Azure OpenAI not in region → allow processing outside the geographic region.

questions.stem:
Copilot gives vague answers about a model with columns such as Amt, Cust_Nm and Dt_1.

What should you do first?

options.text: Rename fields clearly and add descriptions and synonyms

questions.explanation: Copilot works from the model's metadata. Clear field names, descriptions and synonyms (with a clean star schema and hidden technical columns) are the main ways to prepare a model for better answers.
questions.takeaway: Better Copilot answers → clear names, descriptions, synonyms.

questions.stem:
You want Copilot to ignore technical helper tables and columns, and to follow business rules such as 'fiscal year starts in July' when answering.

Which feature should you use?
questions.explanation: Prep data for AI lets model authors simplify the schema Copilot sees (AI data schema), add AI instructions with business context, and provide verified answers for common questions.
questions.takeaway: Steer Copilot on a model → Prep data for AI (schema, instructions, verified answers).

questions.stem: For each statement about Copilot in Power BI, select Yes if it is true.
statements: Copilot respects row-level security for the user asking the question.
Copilot can help write DAX queries in DAX query view.
Copilot edits the source data to correct values it thinks are wrong.
questions.explanation: Copilot works with the user's own permissions, so RLS and access rules still apply to its answers. It can write and explain DAX queries in DAX query view. It doesn't change the semantic model's data; review what it produces before relying on it.
questions.takeaway: Copilot respects permissions; helps with DAX; doesn't change source data.

questions.stem:
A report reader in the service wants a quick written summary of the report page they're viewing.

What can they do?

options.text: Ask Copilot in the service to summarise the page

questions.explanation: In the Copilot pane in the service, readers can ask Copilot to summarise the current page (or report). It doesn't change the report.
questions.takeaway: Readers can ask Copilot for summaries of pages.

questions.stem:
You want Copilot answers to a common question, such as 'What were total sales last quarter?', to always use a specific visual you've approved.

What should you set up?
questions.explanation: Verified answers (part of Prep data for AI) link a visual to trigger phrases, so Copilot returns that approved visual when users ask matching questions.
questions.takeaway: Approved responses to common questions → verified answers.

questions.stem:
Report readers keep asking how to use a page's slicers and buttons.

What is a simple built-in way to guide them on the page?

options.text: Add an info button or help overlay that explains the page

questions.explanation: A text box or an information button with a tooltip (or a bookmark that shows a help overlay) explains the page in place. Many reports add an 'i' button that toggles a help layer with bookmarks.
questions.takeaway: In-report guidance → text, info buttons, help overlays.

questions.stem:
A report has detail pages that should only be reached through drillthrough, not from the page tabs.

What should you do?

options.text: Delete the pages and recreate them as reports

questions.explanation: Hide those pages. Hidden pages don't appear as tabs in reading view, but drillthrough, buttons and bookmarks can still reach them.
questions.takeaway: Pages for drillthrough or tooltips only → hide them.

questions.stem:
The matrix in the exhibit shows sales by category and product. Users want to see the products only for the category they're interested in, without expanding every category.

What should they do?

image.alt: Matrix showing collapsed categories Apparel, Bags and Footwear with plus icons, and a total.

options.text: Drill down into the selected category

questions.explanation: Turn on drill mode and select one category to drill down into its products, or use the +/- icons to expand one category. Expand all down one level would show every category's products.
questions.takeaway: One branch only → drill down or expand that single item.

questions.stem:
You want readers to be able to switch a chart between showing sales by Region, by Channel or by Product, using a slicer.

What should you create?
questions.explanation: A field parameter with Region, Channel and Product lets a slicer swap the field on the chart's axis. Bookmarks would need three copies of the chart.
questions.takeaway: Let readers swap a visual's field → field parameter.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem: Select the least-privileged workspace role for each person.

parts.label: Can delete the workspace and add other Admins
Publishes and edits reports but doesn't share or manage the app
Publishes and updates the workspace app and adds Contributors
Only reads and interacts with reports

questions.explanation: Viewer can only view and interact. Contributor can create, edit and delete content. Member can also share, publish or update the app, and add Members, Contributors and Viewers. Only Admin can delete the workspace, change its settings or add Admins.
questions.takeaway: View → Viewer. Edit → Contributor. Share/app/add people → Member. Settings/delete/Admins → Admin.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a workspace's Manage access panel. Priya must be able to add other people to the workspace, using the least privilege.

Which role should Priya have?

image.alt: Manage access for the Sales Analytics workspace: Finance Admins group as Admin, Priya Nair as Contributor (selected), Sales Team group as Viewer.

questions.explanation: Contributors can't add people. Members can add Members, Contributors and Viewers, which meets the requirement without the extra rights of Admin.
questions.takeaway: Add people (not Admins) → Member.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
Several people need the same workspace role, and staff join and leave often.

What is the best way to grant access?

options.text: Share the workspace link by email
Add a security group to the role

questions.explanation: Assign the role to a Microsoft Entra security group (or Microsoft 365 group). Membership changes are then handled by the group, not by editing workspace access.
questions.takeaway: Grant access to groups, not individuals.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
A workspace is on shared capacity (Pro). Free-licensed users report that they can't open its reports.

What would let free users view the content without buying each of them a Pro licence?

options.text: Move the workspace to Premium per user
Share the reports with Publish to web
Give the users the Viewer role
Move the workspace to Premium capacity or Fabric F64 or larger

questions.explanation: On shared capacity, both creators and viewers need Pro (or PPU) licences. Content in a workspace on Premium capacity (P SKU) or Fabric capacity F64 or larger can be viewed by free users. Premium per user doesn't help, since every viewer would need PPU.
questions.takeaway: Free viewers → content on P SKU or F64+ capacity.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
An analyst publishes reports to My workspace and wants colleagues to collaborate on them.

What should the analyst do?

options.text: Create a shared workspace and publish there
Give colleagues the Viewer role in My workspace

questions.explanation: My workspace is for personal content; you can't add collaborators to it. Create a shared workspace, assign roles, and publish there.
questions.takeaway: Collaboration → a shared workspace, not My workspace.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
You want report and semantic model definitions in a workspace to be version-controlled, with changes committed to a repository.

What should you configure?
questions.explanation: Git integration connects a workspace to an Azure DevOps or GitHub repository, so items can be committed, compared and restored. Saving copies of .pbix files by hand doesn't give real version history.
questions.takeaway: Version control for workspace items → Git integration.

questions.stem:
You publish a workspace app. Later you update a report in the workspace, but app users still see the old version.

What should you do?

options.text: Reinstall the app for each user

questions.explanation: An app is a published snapshot. Changes in the workspace reach app users only when someone with the right role selects Update app.
questions.takeaway: Workspace changes reach app users only after Update app.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows an app's audience setup. The Finance audience must not see the Pipeline report.

What should you do?

image.alt: App audience settings with Sales and Finance audiences. Finance is selected and currently sees Revenue Overview, Pipeline and Budget vs Actual.

options.text: Hide the Pipeline report in the Finance audience

questions.explanation: In the Finance audience, hide the Pipeline report (each audience controls which content its members see). Content hidden from an audience is still available to other audiences.
questions.takeaway: Different content per group in one app → audiences.

questions.stem:
App users want to build their own reports in Excel and Power BI Desktop using the app's semantic model.

What should you set when publishing the app?

options.text: Allow users to build content with the semantic models in the app permissions

questions.explanation: In the app's permissions, allow audience members to build content with the underlying semantic models. That grants Build permission without giving them a workspace role.
questions.takeaway: App users building their own content → allow Build in app permissions.

questions.stem: Why distribute content to a large audience through an app rather than giving everyone a workspace role?

options.text: Apps separate a curated view for readers from the working workspace

questions.explanation: Apps give readers a curated, navigable package, separate what they see from work in progress in the workspace, and support audiences. Workspace roles are for people who work on the content.
questions.takeaway: Consumers → app. Creators → workspace roles.

questions.stem:
You share a report with a colleague and want them to view it but not share it with anyone else.

What should you do in the share dialog?

options.text: Clear Allow recipients to share this report

questions.explanation: Clear Allow recipients to share this report. They can view and interact but can't reshare. Build permission is a separate check box.
questions.takeaway: Stop resharing → clear the reshare option when sharing.

questions.stem: Select the sharing approach for each requirement.

parts.label: Show a report inside an internal SharePoint Online page, respecting each viewer's access
Publish public census statistics on the company's public website
Let a partner company's staff view a report securely with their own work accounts

questions.explanation: Publish to web makes a report public to anyone with the link, with no sign-in or security, so it's only for public data. Embedding in SharePoint Online keeps Power BI sign-in and permissions. Microsoft Entra B2B guest access lets external partners sign in with their own accounts.
questions.takeaway: Public data → Publish to web. Intranet → SharePoint embed. External partners → B2B guests.

questions.stem:
A colleague asks for a Publish to web link for a report that contains customer revenue.

What should you advise?

options.text: Don't use it: anyone with the link could see the data, with no sign-in
It's fine, because Publish to web respects RLS
It's fine if the link is sent only by email
Use it, but set a sensitivity label

questions.explanation: Publish to web creates a public link that anyone on the internet can open without signing in, and it can't apply RLS. It's only for data meant to be public. Use sharing, an app or a secure embed instead.
questions.takeaway: Publish to web = public internet. Never for confidential data.

questions.stem:
A user wants to analyse a published semantic model in an Excel PivotTable connected live to it.

What do they need?

options.text: Build permission on the semantic model

questions.explanation: Analyze in Excel connects Excel to the semantic model and requires Build permission (or a workspace role that includes it). The PivotTable then uses the model's measures, and RLS applies.
questions.takeaway: Analyze in Excel → Build permission on the semantic model.

questions.stem:
You need to see everyone who has access to a semantic model, including access through apps and direct sharing, and remove one person's Build permission.

Where should you go?

options.text: The semantic model's Manage permissions page

questions.explanation: The semantic model's Manage permissions page lists direct access, access through apps and links, with each person's permissions (Read, Build, Reshare), and lets you remove them.
questions.takeaway: Review and change item-level access → Manage permissions.

questions.stem:
Managers want a report page emailed to them every Monday at 8 AM, with the page attached as a PDF.

What should you create?

options.text: A Power Automate flow with no trigger

questions.explanation: A report subscription emails a snapshot of selected pages on a schedule and can attach the report as PDF or PowerPoint. Alerts are triggered by thresholds, not schedules.
questions.takeaway: Scheduled emails of report pages → subscription.

questions.stem:
Each regional manager should receive the same subscription email, but filtered to their own region, without you creating one subscription per manager.

What should you use?
questions.explanation: A dynamic per-recipient subscription reads recipients and their filter values (such as Region) from a semantic model table, so each person gets their own filtered version from a single subscription.
questions.takeaway: One subscription, personalised per person → dynamic per-recipient subscription.

questions.stem:
A data alert on a dashboard card fires when sales drop below 1 million. The operations team also wants a Teams message posted automatically each time.

What should you do?

options.text: Trigger a Power Automate flow from the alert
Subscribe the Teams channel to the report

questions.explanation: Data alerts can trigger a Power Automate flow (using the Power BI alert trigger), which can post to Teams, send emails or start other processes.
questions.takeaway: Act automatically on an alert → Power Automate.

questions.stem:
You want a dashboard tile that shows an entire report page, including its slicers, and stays interactive.

What should you pin?
questions.explanation: Pin a live page: the whole page becomes one tile that updates and keeps the page's slicers and interactions within the tile. Pinning individual visuals creates separate static tiles, and slicers can't be pinned alone.
questions.takeaway: Whole interactive page on a dashboard → pin a live page.

questions.stem:
A dashboard tile's title must change, and clicking the tile should open a different report page than the one it was pinned from.

Where do you change these?

options.text: Edit the original visual and re-pin

questions.explanation: Tile details (from the tile's More options) let you change the title and subtitle and set a custom link, such as another report page or a web address.
questions.takeaway: Change a tile's title or click target → Edit details on the tile.

questions.stem:
Finance needs an invoice-style report that prints cleanly across many pages, with headers repeated on every page.

Which tool do you use to create it?
questions.explanation: Paginated reports are built in Power BI Report Builder. They're designed for pixel-perfect, page-by-page layouts that print and export reliably, with repeating headers and footers.
questions.takeaway: Printable, multi-page layouts → paginated report in Power BI Report Builder.

questions.stem: Which requirement is the clearest sign you need a paginated report rather than a Power BI report?

options.text: Users drill down and cross-filter visuals
A 300-page customer statement, exported to Word and Excel with exact layout

questions.explanation: Paginated reports suit operational outputs that run to many pages, such as statements or invoices, and need exports to Word, Excel, CSV or XML with exact layout. Interactive exploration is what Power BI reports do best.
questions.takeaway: Many printable pages and exact exports → paginated.

questions.stem:
A paginated report must let users choose a customer before it runs, then show only that customer's statement.

What should you add?
questions.explanation: Report parameters prompt users for values (here a customer) and filter the dataset query. They're the main way to make paginated reports interactive.
questions.takeaway: Paginated report filtering by user choice → report parameter.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a semantic model's refresh history.

What has Power BI done after the latest failure, and why?

image.alt: Refresh history with four scheduled refreshes from 6 to 9 October that each failed with invalid credentials, followed by a row saying the schedule was disabled after too many consecutive failures.

options.text: Retried every hour until it succeeded
Turned off scheduled refresh because it failed four times in a row

questions.explanation: After four consecutive scheduled refresh failures, Power BI disables the refresh schedule and notifies the owner. Fix the cause (here, credentials), then turn the schedule back on.
questions.takeaway: Four consecutive failures → schedule disabled.

questions.stem:
A semantic model uses an on-premises SQL Server through a gateway. Refresh fails with 'The data source is missing a gateway connection'.

What should you do?

options.text: Map the data source to a gateway connection in the semantic model's settings

questions.explanation: In the semantic model's settings, under Gateway and cloud connections, map the data source to a gateway connection (creating the connection on the gateway first if needed). Republishing doesn't create the mapping.
questions.takeaway: Missing gateway connection → map the source to a connection in the model's settings.

questions.stem:
Several critical semantic models depend on one on-premises gateway server. If it goes down, all refreshes fail.

What should you set up?

options.text: A personal-mode gateway for each analyst
Additional gateway members in a cluster

questions.explanation: A gateway cluster: install additional gateway members in the same cluster on other servers, so refreshes continue if one member is unavailable.
questions.takeaway: Gateway high availability → a gateway cluster.

questions.stem:
A semantic model must refresh as soon as the nightly ETL (extract, transform, load) job finishes, which varies between 2 AM and 5 AM.

What should you use?

options.text: Trigger the refresh when the ETL job completes

questions.explanation: Trigger the refresh when the job finishes, for example from the ETL pipeline or a Power Automate flow calling the refresh action or API. A fixed schedule would either run too early or wait unnecessarily.
questions.takeaway: Refresh after an upstream job → trigger it (pipeline, Power Automate or API).

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows lineage view. You plan to remove a column from the Sales semantic model.

What should you check first?

image.alt: Lineage view: SQL Server feeds the Sales semantic model, which feeds the Sales Overview and Regional Detail reports; Sales Overview feeds the Exec Dashboard.

options.text: Impact analysis for the semantic model

questions.explanation: Impact analysis on the semantic model shows downstream reports, dashboards and workspaces that depend on it (and lets you notify their contacts), so you can see what the change might break. Lineage view already shows two reports and a dashboard downstream.
questions.takeaway: Before changing a shared model → impact analysis.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem: Select the endorsement that fits each situation.

parts.label: The model's owner thinks it's ready for others to reuse
A governance team has reviewed the model against company standards
The single authoritative source of customer reference data

questions.explanation: Promoted means the owner thinks the item is ready to share. Certified means an authorised reviewer has checked it against organisational standards. Master data marks the authoritative source for core reference data, such as the customer master list.
questions.takeaway: Promoted = owner's endorsement. Certified = official review. Master data = core reference data.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem: Who can certify a semantic model?

options.text: People authorised by the admin in the tenant's certification setting

questions.explanation: Only users or groups the Power BI (Fabric) admin has authorised in the tenant's certification setting can certify content. Workspace roles alone aren't enough.
questions.takeaway: Certify → people authorised in tenant settings.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a deployment pipeline. You changed one report in Development.

What happens when you deploy from Development to Test?

image.alt: Deployment pipeline: Development (1 item changed), Test and Production, each with a Sales model and two reports. Development and Test are marked Different; Test and Production are marked Same.

options.text: The change goes straight to Production
The changed content is copied to the Test workspace
Only the data is copied, not the report

questions.explanation: Deploying copies the selected (or changed) content from the source stage to the target stage's workspace. The comparison indicator shows the stages differ. Production is untouched until you deploy from Test.
questions.takeaway: Deploy = copy content to the next stage's workspace; later stages are unaffected.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
In a deployment pipeline, the Production stage must automatically use the production database and a parameter value of Prod.

What should you configure?

options.text: Deployment rules for the Production stage

questions.explanation: Deployment rules on the Production stage (data source rules and parameter rules) change the connection and parameter values whenever content is deployed into that stage.
questions.takeaway: Per-stage connections or parameters → deployment rules.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem: Which workspaces can be assigned to deployment pipeline stages?

options.text: Workspaces on Premium per user, Premium or Fabric capacity

questions.explanation: Deployment pipelines need workspaces on Premium per user, Premium capacity or Fabric capacity. Shared-capacity (Pro) workspaces can't be assigned to stages.
questions.takeaway: Deployment pipelines → Premium, PPU or Fabric workspaces.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
Your organisation requires every report and semantic model to have a sensitivity label before it's saved or published.

What should the admin configure?
questions.explanation: A mandatory labeling policy (set up in Microsoft Purview and enabled for Power BI) forces users to apply a label. A default label can also be applied automatically, but mandatory labeling is what enforces the requirement.
questions.takeaway: Labels required → mandatory labeling policy.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem: A report has the Highly Confidential label, which includes encryption. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
statements: An exported Excel file keeps the label's protection.
Labels can be applied in Power BI Desktop as well as in the service.
The label restricts which rows each user sees in the report.
questions.explanation: Supported exports, such as Excel, PowerPoint and PDF, carry the label and its protection, so only authorised people can open them. Labels are defined in Microsoft Purview and applied in Power BI Desktop or the service. A label doesn't filter rows; that's RLS.
questions.takeaway: Labels classify and protect exported files; they don't filter data.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A semantic model has the Confidential label. You create a new report on it in the service.

What happens to the report's label?

options.text: The report has no label until someone adds one
The report inherits the Confidential label

questions.explanation: With downstream inheritance enabled, new content created from a labelled semantic model inherits its label (unless a label was set manually). This keeps classification consistent.
questions.takeaway: Downstream inheritance → new content inherits the model's label.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
An admin wants to stop users from exporting underlying data from reports across the organisation.

Where is this controlled?

options.text: Tenant settings in the admin portal

questions.explanation: Export settings are tenant settings in the admin portal (with options such as allowing only summarized data). Report authors can also restrict export per report, but organisation-wide control is in tenant settings.
questions.takeaway: Organisation-wide export rules → admin portal tenant settings.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
You need to know how often a report was viewed in the last 30 days and by how many users.

What should you open?
questions.explanation: The report's usage metrics report shows views, unique viewers and page usage over recent days. Lineage view and refresh history don't track viewing.
questions.takeaway: Who's viewing → usage metrics.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A semantic model in another workspace must be used by your report, but you don't have a role in that workspace.

Which permission lets you connect to it from Power BI Desktop?

options.text: The Viewer role in your own workspace
Build permission on the semantic model

questions.explanation: Build permission on the semantic model lets you discover it, connect from Desktop (as a live connection or composite model) and build reports, without any role in its workspace.
questions.takeaway: Use someone else's model → Build permission.

questions.stem: Which data sources need an on-premises data gateway for scheduled refresh?
questions.explanation: Only the on-premises SQL Server holding StockLevel is inside the company network. Azure SQL Database and SharePoint Online are cloud sources the service reaches directly.
questions.takeaway: Gateway only for sources inside the company network.

questions.stem: How should you configure the Sales table to meet the freshness and performance requirements while keeping refresh times practical?

options.text: Import with a full refresh every night

questions.explanation: Data only needs to be current by 7 AM, so Import gives the fastest visuals, and incremental refresh avoids reloading 900 million rows every night by refreshing only recent partitions. DirectQuery would slow every visual.
questions.takeaway: Daily freshness + fast visuals + huge fact → Import with incremental refresh.

questions.stem: Which measure meets the inventory requirement?
questions.explanation: Stock on hand is semi-additive: it adds across stores and products but not across days. Evaluating the sum on the last date of the period gives the closing stock for any month, quarter or year. StockLevel has a row every day, so LASTDATE always finds data.
questions.takeaway: Closing stock → sum on the period's last date.

questions.stem: How should the Targets table be related so that targets can be compared with sales by category and month?

options.text: One-to-many from Targets to Product on Category
Many-to-many between Product[Category] and Targets[Category], with Product filtering Targets, plus a month-level link to Date

questions.explanation: Targets are at category-and-month grain, while Product is at product grain, so Category isn't unique on either side.
