Microsoft's pattern is a many-to-many relationship from Product[Category] to Targets[Category] with Product filtering Targets, plus a month-level link to Date, and keeping target visuals at month level or above.
questions.takeaway: Higher-grain facts → many-to-many on the shared attribute, single direction.

questions.stem: How should you meet the security requirements for regional directors with the least ongoing maintenance?

options.text: One static role per region, edited whenever coverage changes
A director-region mapping table with a dynamic role using USERPRINCIPALNAME ()

questions.explanation: Directors can cover several regions and coverage changes, so a mapping table (one row per director per region) with a dynamic role using USERPRINCIPALNAME () handles it: changes are new rows, not new roles. Executives get a role with no filter; store managers use a dynamic role on ManagerEmail.
questions.takeaway: Many-to-many user access that changes → mapping table + dynamic role.

questions.stem: How should you distribute reports to the store managers?

options.text: Give each manager the Viewer role

questions.explanation: A workspace app gives managers a curated set of reports separate from the workspace's work in progress (audiences can tailor content). Because the workspace is on F64, free-licensed users can view it. Viewer roles would expose the workspace itself.
questions.takeaway: Curated content for many free-licence readers → app on F64+ capacity.

questions.stem: For each statement about the store managers' access, select Yes if it is true.
statements: Store managers with free licences can view the app because the workspace is on F64.
Store managers see every store when they open the app, because apps bypass RLS.
Row-level security applies to store managers when they view reports in the app.
questions.explanation: F64 capacity lets free users view content. Store managers aren't added to the executives' role, so RLS restricts them to their store. RLS applies in apps just as in the workspace.
questions.takeaway: F64+ capacity: free viewers. RLS follows users into apps.

questions.stem: Which storage mode should the semantic model use?
questions.explanation: The data is in Delta tables in OneLake and must be near-current with Import-like speed and no import copies. Direct Lake reads the Delta files directly into memory. Import would copy 300 million rows; DirectQuery would be slower.
questions.takeaway: Fabric Delta tables + no copies + fast → Direct Lake.

questions.stem: Which feature meets the requirement for PatientName and DateOfBirth?

options.text: Hide the columns in report view

questions.explanation: Object-level security hides those columns from analysts entirely (they can't see or query them) while clinical managers' role allows them. RLS filters rows, which isn't needed: analysts must see every appointment.
questions.takeaway: Hide columns from some users → object-level security.

questions.stem: What should the admin configure so that every report and semantic model has a sensitivity label before publishing?
questions.explanation: A mandatory labeling policy in Microsoft Purview, enabled for Power BI, requires a label on content. A default label alone doesn't force users to choose an appropriate one.
questions.takeaway: Required labels → mandatory labeling policy.

questions.stem: Which visual best meets the analysts' no-show requirement?
questions.explanation: Key influencers ranks the factors (booking channel, lead time, age band and so on) associated with NoShow being Yes, and Top segments finds combinations of them. A decomposition tree breaks totals down rather than ranking drivers.
questions.takeaway: What drives an outcome → Key influencers.

questions.stem: How should you meet the operations managers' requirement?

options.text: Anomaly detection on a line chart of daily appointments
A data alert on a table visual

questions.explanation: Turn on anomaly detection for a line chart of daily appointments (from the Analytics pane), optionally with Explain by fields such as Clinic. Unusual days are flagged against the expected range.
questions.takeaway: Flag unusual points over time → anomaly detection on a line chart.

questions.stem: For each statement about the executives' requirement, select Yes if it is true.
statements: A narrative visual with Copilot can provide the summary.
Copilot requires an admin tenant setting and a workspace on supported paid capacity.
Copilot lets analysts see PatientName in its answers, because it bypasses object-level security.
questions.explanation: A narrative visual with Copilot can write and refresh the summary. Copilot needs the tenant setting enabled and a workspace on supported paid capacity, which Contoso's Fabric capacity can provide. Copilot answers respect each user's permissions, so OLS still hides patient columns from analysts.
questions.takeaway: Copilot: tenant setting + capacity; respects security.

questions.stem: How should you support on-time % by delivery month alongside counts by order month?

options.text: Add an inactive DeliveredDate relationship and use USERELATIONSHIP in the on-time measure
Merge DeliveredDate into the Date table

questions.explanation: Add an inactive relationship from DeliveredDate to Date and write the on-time measure with USERELATIONSHIP, keeping OrderDate as the active relationship for shipment counts. (A separate Delivery Date table would also work, but the measure-level approach meets this requirement with less change.)
questions.takeaway: Second date role in specific measures → inactive relationship + USERELATIONSHIP.

questions.stem: Which measure returns the on-time %, counting only delivered shipments?

options.text: `DIVIDE ( COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( Shipments, NOT ISBLANK ( Shipments[DeliveredDate] ) && Shipments[DeliveredDate] <= Shipments[PromisedDate] ) ), COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( Shipments, NOT ISBLANK ( Shipments[DeliveredDate] ) ) ) )`

questions.explanation: Count delivered shipments whose DeliveredDate is on or before PromisedDate, divide by all delivered shipments, and use DIVIDE for safety. Undelivered shipments (null DeliveredDate, like 90013) must be excluded from both counts.
questions.takeaway: Ratio of qualifying rows → DIVIDE of two filtered counts.

questions.stem: How should you meet the right-click requirement?

options.text: A drillthrough page with Customer in the Drill through well

questions.explanation: Create a Customer Shipments page with Customer in its Drill through well. Users then right-click a customer in any visual and choose Drill through. Tooltips appear on hover, not on right-click.
questions.takeaway: Right-click to a detail page → drillthrough.

questions.stem: How should you meet the notification requirement?

options.text: A data alert on a dashboard card tile

questions.explanation: Pin a card (or KPI or gauge) showing current-month on-time % to a dashboard and set a data alert below 92%. Data alerts work only on dashboard tiles of those types.
questions.takeaway: Threshold notification → data alert on a card, KPI or gauge dashboard tile.

questions.stem: What should you create for the depot manifests?

options.text: A paginated report with a scheduled subscription

questions.explanation: A paginated report (built in Power BI Report Builder) with a subscription that attaches a PDF each morning. It handles long, printable documents with repeated headers; standard report subscriptions export pages, not 200-page documents.
questions.takeaway: Long printable documents on a schedule → paginated report + subscription.

questions.stem: How should you meet the deployment requirement?

options.text: Three copies of the .pbix edited by hand
A deployment pipeline with deployment rules

questions.explanation: A deployment pipeline with Development, Test and Production stages, using deployment rules (data source or parameter rules) so each stage connects to its own database. The workspaces must be on Premium, PPU or Fabric capacity.
questions.takeaway: Dev/Test/Prod with different databases → deployment pipeline + rules.

questions.stem: Which calculation converts transactions to US dollars as required?

options.text: Bring each line's rate (matching currency and date) onto the row, then `SUMX ( Transactions, Transactions[LocalAmount] * Transactions[Rate] )`

questions.explanation: Each line needs its own rate, so convert row by row. A calculated column (or Power Query merge) fetches the rate for the line's currency and date, for example with LOOKUPVALUE, and SUMX of LocalAmount × rate gives the USD total. Multiplying totals by an average rate is wrong whenever rates or currencies vary.
questions.takeaway: Per-row conversion → bring the matching rate to each row, then SUMX.

questions.stem: [Sales USD] exists. Which measure returns fiscal year-to-date sales in US dollars?
questions.explanation: TOTALYTD's year-end argument sets the fiscal year end, "6/30", so the total restarts on 1 July.
questions.takeaway: Fiscal YTD → TOTALYTD with the year-end date.

questions.stem: How should Budget be related to the model so budget can be compared with actual sales by department and month?

options.text: Relate Budget to Department and to Date at month level
Leave Budget unrelated and use slicers

questions.explanation: Budget is at department-and-month grain. Relate it to the Department dimension and to Date at month level (for example a first-of-month date related to Date[Date]), and keep budget comparisons at month level or above in visuals.
questions.takeaway: Monthly budget → relate at month level and avoid day-level visuals.

questions.stem: How should you meet the department heads' email requirement?
questions.explanation: A dynamic per-recipient subscription reads each recipient's email and their department filter from a table, sending each head a filtered version from one subscription.
questions.takeaway: One subscription, filtered per person → dynamic per-recipient subscription.

questions.stem: How should you give finance analysts access to build PivotTables in Excel?

options.text: Grant Build permission on the semantic model
Export the data to CSV each month

questions.explanation: Build permission on the semantic model (without an editing workspace role) lets them use Analyze in Excel. Contributor or Member would let them edit workspace content.
questions.takeaway: Excel PivotTables without edit rights → Build permission.

questions.stem: How should you mark the finance semantic model as the official, reviewed source?

options.text: Have an authorised reviewer certify it

questions.explanation: Certification, by a reviewer authorised in tenant settings, marks the model as meeting organisational standards. Promotion only shows that the owner thinks it's ready.
questions.takeaway: Official and reviewed → certified.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows quarterly sales with a constant line at the 500K target.

For each statement, select Yes if it is true.

image.alt: Column chart: Q1 420K, Q2 530K, Q3 480K, Q4 610K, with a dashed target line at 500K.

statements: Two quarters are above target.
Q3 is above target.
Q4 has the highest sales.
questions.explanation: Q2 (530K) and Q4 (610K) are above the 500K line; Q1 (420K) and Q3 (480K) are below. Q4 is the highest quarter.
questions.takeaway: Read reference lines against each bar's value.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a gauge for monthly support tickets resolved.

For each statement, select Yes if it is true.

image.alt: Gauge from 0 to 12,000 with the arc filled to 8,400 and a target marker at 9,000.

statements: The target has been met.
The maximum value on the gauge is 12,000.
The filled arc represents the current value.
questions.explanation: The value (8,400) hasn't reached the 9,000 target marker. The gauge's maximum is 12,000. The filled arc shows the current value against the range.
questions.takeaway: Gauge: arc = value, marker = target, ends = min and max.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows each region's share of sales per year.

Select the answer that completes each statement.

image.alt: 100% stacked columns for 2023 to 2026. North's share is 44%, 47%, 49%, 49%; South's 34%, 28%, 23%, 19%; West's 22%, 25%, 28%, 32%.

parts.label: The region with the largest share in 2026 is
The region whose share grows every year is

questions.explanation: In a 100% stacked chart, each segment's height is its share of that year. North has the largest share in 2026 (about 49%). West's share rises every year (22% → 25% → 28% → 32%).
questions.takeaway: 100% stacked: compare segment heights as shares.

questions.stem:
The exhibit plots products by units sold and average discount.

For each statement, select Yes if it is true.

image.alt: Scatter chart: Gaiters at 690 units and 6% discount; Daypack at 140 units and 34%; Trail Shoe, Rain Jacket, Sandal and Fleece between 300 and 420 units at 12 to 19%.

statements: Gaiters sells the most units with the smallest discount.
Daypack sells the most units.
Most products have an average discount between 10% and 20%.
questions.explanation: Gaiters sells the most units at the lowest discount, so it doesn't need discounting to sell. Daypack has the highest discount but low units. Most products cluster between 10% and 20% discount.
questions.takeaway: Scatter: read each point on both axes.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a waterfall of cash from the start to the end of the quarter.

Select the answer that completes each statement.

image.alt: Waterfall from an opening balance of 300K: Collections +180K, Payroll −120K, Suppliers −40K, Interest +25K, then the closing balance.

parts.label: The largest increase came from
The ending cash balance is

questions.explanation: Collections (+180K) is the largest increase. The ending balance is 300 + 180 − 120 − 40 + 25 = 345K.
questions.takeaway: Waterfall: start + every step = end.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a matrix with subtotals.

For each statement, select Yes if it is true.

image.alt: Matrix: Footwear 750 (Trail Shoe 500, Sandal 250), Bags 300 (Daypack 300), Apparel 450 (Rain Jacket 450), with the grand total cell left empty.

statements: The Footwear subtotal equals Trail Shoe plus Sandal.
Bags is the category with the lowest sales.
The grand total is 1,200.
questions.explanation: Footwear's subtotal (750) is the sum of its products. Bags (300) is the smallest category. The grand total is 750 + 300 + 450 = 1,500, not 1,200.
questions.takeaway: Matrix subtotals and totals add up the rows beneath them (for additive measures).

questions.stem: Select the visual for each requirement.

parts.label: How the distribution of order values looks (how many orders fall in each value band)
How each product's sales ranking changed month by month
Sales shaded by the company's own sales territories, drawn from a TopoJSON file

questions.explanation: A ribbon chart shows how rankings change between periods. A histogram (a column chart over binned values) shows how values are distributed. A shape map shades custom regions defined by a TopoJSON file, such as sales territories.
questions.takeaway: Rank changes → ribbon. Distribution → binned column. Custom regions → shape map.

questions.stem: Select the visual for each requirement.

parts.label: Total revenue as a single large number
This month's revenue against target, with the monthly trend behind it
Revenue so far as progress between 0 and the annual maximum, with a target marker

questions.explanation: A card shows one number. A KPI visual shows a value compared with a target, with a trend. A gauge shows progress within a range towards a target.
questions.takeaway: One number → card. Value vs target with trend → KPI. Progress in a range → gauge.

questions.stem: Select the Analytics pane line for each requirement.

parts.label: The mean of the values shown
A target returned by a [Target] measure
The middle value, unaffected by a few extreme values
The value below which 90% of the points fall

questions.explanation: Average and median lines are calculated from the data in the visual. A constant line can take a fixed value or a measure through fx. A percentile line marks a chosen percentile, such as the 90th.
questions.takeaway: Analytics lines: average, median, percentile from the data; constant from you or a measure.

questions.stem: Select the approach for each requirement.

parts.label: Users pick a region from a control on the page
Test accounts are excluded from every page
One table shows only customers whose Sales is above 1,000

questions.explanation: Filtering on a measure's value, such as customers with sales over 1,000, is only possible at visual level. Report-level filters apply to every page. Slicers put the choice on the canvas for users.
questions.takeaway: Measure condition → visual filter. Everywhere → report filter. User's choice on canvas → slicer.

questions.stem: A user selects a region in a bar chart. Select the Edit interactions setting for each other visual.

parts.label: A line chart of monthly sales must show only the selected region's trend
A column chart must show the selected region's portion inside each month's total
A card of company-wide revenue must not change

questions.explanation: None leaves a visual unchanged. Highlight keeps the totals visible and highlights the selection within them. Filter shows only the selection, and is the only option for line charts.
questions.takeaway: Unchanged → None. Selection within totals → Highlight. Only the selection → Filter.

questions.stem: Select the setting that meets each requirement.

parts.label: Month names must appear January to December in every visual
options: Set Sort by column to Month Number

parts.label: A bar chart must always show the best-selling product first
options: Sort the visual by Sales, descending
Set Sort by column to Product ID

questions.explanation: To make month names sort in calendar order everywhere, set the column's Sort by column to the month number. To keep a bar chart ranked by value, sort the visual by the measure, descending.
questions.takeaway: Text in a natural order → Sort by column. Rank in one visual → sort the visual by the measure.

questions.stem: Select the quickest way to meet each requirement.

parts.label: Every visual uses the company's brand colours and font
A new chart must look exactly like a chart you've already formatted
Every new page has the same header bar, logo and title position

questions.explanation: A report theme (JSON) sets colours and fonts for every visual. Format painter copies one visual's formatting to another. Duplicating a template page reuses a fixed layout, such as a header and logo.
questions.takeaway: Report-wide style → theme. One visual's style → Format painter. Repeated layout → template page.

questions.stem: For each statement about bookmarks, select Yes if it is true.
statements: A bookmark with the Data property on reapplies slicer selections.
Applying a bookmark refreshes the semantic model.
Readers can create personal bookmarks in the Power BI service.
questions.explanation: With Data turned on, a bookmark captures and reapplies filter and slicer state. Bookmarks don't refresh data. Report readers can create personal bookmarks in the Power BI service.
questions.takeaway: Bookmarks capture state, not data refreshes.

questions.stem: For each statement about drillthrough, select Yes if it is true.
statements: Power BI adds a back button to a drillthrough page automatically.
A drillthrough page can use more than one drillthrough field.
Cross-report drillthrough works between reports that use different semantic models.
questions.explanation: Adding a field to a page's Drill through well adds a back button automatically. A drillthrough page can have several drillthrough fields. Cross-report drillthrough only works between reports that use the same semantic model.
questions.takeaway: Drillthrough: back button added; several fields allowed; cross-report needs the same model.

questions.stem: For each statement about slicers, select Yes if it is true.
statements: A slicer can filter another page without being visible on it.
A slicer can filter directly on a measure's value, such as Sales above 1,000.
A relative date slicer set to the last 7 days updates automatically each day.
questions.explanation: Sync slicers can apply a selection to other pages even where the slicer isn't visible. Slicers work on columns, not on measure values. A relative date slicer moves its window forward automatically.
questions.takeaway: Slicers use columns; sync can be invisible; relative dates roll.

questions.stem: For each statement about conditional formatting, select Yes if it is true.
statements: A table's background colour can be based on a measure that isn't displayed in the table.
Icons are available as conditional formatting in table and matrix visuals.
Conditional formatting changes the values stored in the model.
questions.explanation: Formatting can be based on any field or measure, even one not shown in the visual. Icons are available in tables and matrices. Conditional formatting changes only how values look; the data in the model is untouched.
questions.takeaway: Conditional formatting changes appearance only.

questions.stem: For each statement about accessible reports, select Yes if it is true.
statements: Screen readers read a visual's alt text.
Tab order for keyboard users is set in the Selection pane.
Using red and green alone is enough to show good and bad results.
questions.explanation: Screen readers read alt text. The Selection pane's Tab order sets keyboard navigation. Colour alone isn't enough to convey meaning; add labels, icons or markers.
questions.takeaway: Alt text, tab order, and never colour alone.

questions.stem: For each statement about tooltips, select Yes if it is true.
statements: Fields added to a visual's Tooltips well appear when users hover over it.
A report page tooltip still works when its page is hidden.
A report page tooltip can be used by only one visual.
questions.explanation: Fields in a visual's Tooltips well appear in its default tooltip. A tooltip page can be hidden from the page tabs and still work. One tooltip page can serve many visuals.
questions.takeaway: Tooltips well for default tooltips; tooltip pages are reusable and can be hidden.

questions.stem: For each statement about mobile layouts, select Yes if it is true.
statements: Visuals not added to a page's mobile layout aren't shown on phones in portrait view.
A mobile layout must be created as a separate report.
Phone users can rotate to landscape to see the standard page layout.
questions.explanation: Only visuals placed on a page's mobile layout appear when a phone shows that page in portrait. The mobile layout lives in the same report, not a separate one. Rotating the phone to landscape shows the standard layout.
questions.takeaway: Mobile layout = per page, inside the same report.

questions.stem:
You need a mini chart to appear when users hover over a product in a bar chart.

Select the actions you should perform and arrange them in order.

items.text: Add a new page
In Page information, turn on Allow use as tooltip and set the canvas to Tooltip size
Add the mini chart to the page
On the bar chart, set Tooltip type to Report page and select the new page
Add Product to the Drill through well
Create a bookmark of the page

questions.explanation: Create the page, turn on Allow use as tooltip (and set a small canvas), build the mini chart, then on the bar chart set Tooltip type to Report page and choose the new page. Drillthrough and bookmarks aren't involved.
questions.takeaway: Tooltip page → allow as tooltip → build → assign to the visual.

questions.stem:
You need two buttons that switch between showing a chart and a table in the same position.

Select the actions you should perform and arrange them in order.

items.text: Place the chart and the table in the same position
Hide the table in the Selection pane, then add a bookmark named Chart view
Show the table and hide the chart, then add a bookmark named Table view
Turn off the Data property for both bookmarks
Set each button's action to its bookmark
Create a drillthrough page
Turn on Auto date/time

questions.explanation: Place both visuals, set visibility in the Selection pane and capture a bookmark for each state (with Data off so slicers aren't reset), then assign each bookmark to a button.
questions.takeaway: Set visibility → bookmark each state → link buttons.

questions.stem:
Users need a slicer to switch a column chart's axis between Region, Channel and Product.

Select the actions you should perform and arrange them in order.

items.text: Select Modeling > New parameter > Fields
Add Region, Channel and Product, and keep Add slicer to this page selected
Put the new parameter field on the column chart's X-axis
Create a calculation group
Create three bookmarks

questions.explanation: Create a field parameter with the three fields (Modeling > New parameter > Fields), keep the option to add a slicer, then put the parameter on the chart's axis. A calculation group changes measures, not axis fields.
questions.takeaway: New parameter > Fields → slicer → parameter on the axis.

questions.stem:
You need a line chart of monthly sales repeated for each region in a grid.

Select the actions you should perform and arrange them in order.

items.text: Add a line chart
Put Month on the X-axis and Sales on the Y-axis
Add Region to the Small multiples well
Set the grid's rows and columns in the Format pane
Add Region to the Legend
Create one line chart per region

questions.explanation: Add a line chart, put Month on the X-axis and Sales on the Y-axis, add Region to Small multiples, then adjust the grid layout in the Format pane.
questions.takeaway: Small multiples: build the chart, then add the splitting field.

questions.stem:
Analysts want to break down total Sales by Region and Channel, then let Power BI choose the next level automatically.

Select the actions you should perform and arrange them in order.

items.text: Add a decomposition tree visual
Put Sales in Analyze, and Region, Channel and Product in Explain by
Expand the root by Region, then a region by Channel
Select + on a channel and choose High value
Turn on anomaly detection
Add Sales to the Tooltips well

questions.explanation: Add the visual, put Sales in Analyze and the candidate fields in Explain by, expand by Region and Channel, then use the + on a node and choose High value to let AI pick the next level.
questions.takeaway: Analyze + Explain by → expand → AI split.

tabs.title: Overview
paragraphs: Tailwind Traders runs 140 home-improvement stores in four regions. It is moving store and regional reporting from spreadsheets to Power BI.
All reports will be published to one workspace, Retail Analytics, on Fabric capacity F64.

tabs.title: Data sources
paragraphs: Sales: an Azure SQL database. The Sales table has one row per receipt line (about 900 million rows) with StoreKey, ProductKey, DateKey, Quantity and Amount.
Inventory: an on-premises SQL Server. The StockLevel table records each product's stock on hand at each store at the end of every day.
Targets: an Excel workbook in SharePoint Online with one row per product category per month.
Store: a table in the Azure SQL database with StoreKey, StoreName, Region and ManagerEmail. Each store has one manager.

tabs.title: Requirements
paragraphs: Data must be current as of 7:00 AM each day, and visuals must respond quickly.

Store managers must see only their own store. Regional directors must see every store in their region; a director can cover more than one region, and coverage changes several times a year. Executives must see everything.
Inventory reports must show stock on hand at the end of each month, quarter and year.
Sales must be compared with targets by category and month.
The 400 store managers have free Power BI licences. They must get a single, curated set of reports that's separate from work in progress in the workspace.

tabs.title: Exhibit
paragraphs: The current draft model is shown below.

image.alt: Draft model: Store, Product and Date each relate one-to-many to Sales. StockLevel (StoreKey, ProductKey, DateKey, OnHand) has no relationships yet.

tabs.title: Overview
paragraphs: Contoso Clinics operates 35 outpatient clinics. Its data team uses Microsoft Fabric.
Analysts want to understand appointment no-shows and track daily patient volumes.

tabs.title: Data
paragraphs: Appointments: a Delta table in a Fabric lakehouse, updated every 15 minutes, with one row per appointment (about 300 million rows). Columns include PatientKey, ClinicKey, DateKey, BookingChannel, LeadTimeDays, AgeBand and NoShow (Yes or No).
Patient: a lakehouse table with PatientKey, PatientName, DateOfBirth and PostalCode.
Clinic and Date dimension tables are also in the lakehouse.

tabs.title: Requirements
paragraphs: Reports must show near-current data without copying it through scheduled imports, with Import-like performance.
Analysts must see every appointment but must not be able to see or query PatientName or DateOfBirth. Clinical managers must see them.
Every report and semantic model must carry a sensitivity label before it is published.
Analysts need to find which factors make a no-show more likely.
Operations managers want unusual daily appointment volumes flagged automatically.
Executives want an AI-written summary on the overview page.

tabs.title: Overview
paragraphs: Litware Logistics delivers parcels for retailers across three countries. Its operations team wants to monitor on-time delivery.

tabs.title: Data
paragraphs: Shipments: one row per shipment with ShipmentID, CustomerKey, OrderDate, ShipDate, PromisedDate, DeliveredDate and Weight.
A Date table is marked as a date table. Shipments currently has an active relationship from OrderDate to Date.
A shipment is late when DeliveredDate is after PromisedDate.

tabs.title: Requirements
paragraphs: Report on-time delivery % by delivery month, and shipment counts by order month on the same page.
Users must be able to right-click a customer and open a page listing that customer's shipments.
The operations manager must be notified when on-time delivery for the current month drops below 92%.
Each depot must receive a printable delivery manifest of 20 to 200 pages every morning as PDF.
Reports move from Development to Test to Production. Each stage must use its own database.

tabs.title: Exhibit
paragraphs: A sample of the Shipments table.

image.alt: Sample shipments: 90011 delivered on its promised date, 90012 delivered two days late, 90013 not yet delivered (DeliveredDate null).

tabs.title: Overview
paragraphs: Wide World Importers sells goods in several currencies. Finance reports in US dollars. The financial year runs from 1 July to 30 June.

tabs.title: Data
paragraphs: Transactions: one row per invoice line, with InvoiceDate, Currency and LocalAmount.
Rates: one row per currency per day, with Currency, Date and RateToUSD.
Budget: one row per department per month, in US dollars.
A Date table marked as a date table includes FiscalYear and FiscalQuarter columns.

tabs.title: Requirements
paragraphs: Show fiscal year-to-date sales in US dollars.
Each transaction must be converted using the rate for its own currency and date.
Compare actual sales with budget by department and month.
Each department head receives a monthly email of the report filtered to their department, from a single subscription.
Finance analysts must build their own PivotTables in Excel on the semantic model, and must not be able to edit workspace content.
Users must be able to tell that the finance semantic model is the official, reviewed source.
